ballots.fatal_flaw: The normative core relocates, unverified, to the one component with no executable spec: evidence-collect.sh must be built against an evidence.json schema that the agents invent by hand-transcribing prose into ~40 fixtures BEFORE any collector or real gate run exists, and nothing in the design ever validates that invented schema against GitHub's actual API responses.
ballots.attack_trace: Build sequence per the proposal's own migration: commit 1 hand-authors ~40 evidence.json fixtures from the 280-line prose (full LabeledEvent/UnlabeledEvent timelines, old-coordinate diff hunks, MarkedAsDuplicateEvent chains, commit signature-verification objects) — but this gate has never executed once, prerequisites #419/#420/#510/#511/#649 are open, and several fixture scenarios (a VALID roster-human signature commit, a transitive duplicate chain, a strip-then-close sequence) have never occurred in this repo's history, so the promised 'recorded GraphQL response fixtures' for the collector are ALSO invented, not recorded. Commit 2 greens gate-core against that invented schema; the fixture suite is then permanently green and self-referential. When evidence-collect.sh is finally written against the real API (per-issue timelineItems pagination fan-out, closedByPullRequestsReferences per-issue queries, signature-object variants, cross-repo duplicate targets), every shape mismatch is resolved by silently bending the collector's normalization — the exact layer where this factory has already shipped its one proven bug class (#419/#420: the bare 30-item-page counting bug that became a gate prerequisite). Result: a real run yields a byte-replayable, hash-acknowledged, 'correct' verdict over wrong facts, all 26 rounds' guarantees void while tests/run-suite.sh stays green forever. The proposal's own biggestRisk concedes exactly this seam; compounding it, the same migration demands fixtures + four new modules + a coverage-floor ADR inside one PR built by loop agents under CI timeouts — the largest single deliverable the loop has ever attempted, judged by a test suite that cannot detect the failure mode that matters.

ballots.fatal_flaw: The roster chain-of-custody criterion is unsatisfiable under this repo's own sanctioned merge mechanism and has no remediation path: in a squash-only repo where agents (and even the human, via the UI) merge through GitHub, every MAINTAINERS.md-touching commit on the default branch is committed and signed by GitHub's web-flow key, so signature.signer.login resolves to web-flow — never to a 'Human maintainers' roster account.
ballots.attack_trace: Operational sequence: MAINTAINERS.md today lists exactly ONE human (MrEyratnz); the design's universal-witness rule makes that one person a hard serial dependency for every release with any gate-relevant close (first ledger: the ~465-finding review-loop blowup), so the first thing a sane operator does is add a second human maintainer. That edit lands the only way this factory lands anything — a squash-merged PR (repo law; agents merge autonomously via GitHub App identities). The resulting default-branch commit's committer is web-flow and its verified signature is GitHub's web-flow key: 'VALID', but signer.login is not on the roster. The gate's history walk from the 2026-07-29 pin now finds a roster change failing the criterion — and unlike every close binding, which the proposal carefully gives the #894 remediation cure, a roster commit is immutable history with no cure defined and 'never an override' as explicit doctrine: the gate is bricked until history rewrite or a spec amendment. The only compliant write path — a human pushing a locally GPG-signed commit straight to the default branch — bypasses PR review, the hooks, and 'CI is the authoritative gate', i.e. the criterion can only be satisfied by violating the factory's other laws. On build cost the proposal is also strictly a superset: it keeps every interval-algebra/hunk-parser/duplicate-chain/signature binding as a hard precondition ('net simpler' counts deleted prose branches, not implementation surface), then adds the roster walk on top — the god-spec plus one criterion that deadlocks.

ballots.fatal_flaw: The entire anti-laundering guarantee is moved onto the nightly close-auditor, but the gate never verifies the auditor is alive: criterion 6 requires only 'deployed with >=1 successful run' — a one-time historical check — and the gate-report carries only 'the latest' audit summary with no freshness predicate, so the gate passes green with the auditor dead since its first run.
ballots.attack_trace: Failure sequence, fully inside the proposal's own text: (1) close-audit.yml succeeds once at deployment — criterion 6 is satisfied forever after. (2) The auditor then breaks silently (token permission rotation, GraphQL schema drift, the same 30-item pagination class as #419/#420 — nightly jobs in this repo have no watcher, and no criterion re-checks them). (3) An agent closes a P0 tech-debt issue 'not planned'. Heuristic (a) would have reopened it, but the auditor never runs. (4) Release time: criteria 1–5 are current-state-only by design — the closed issue is invisible; criterion 6 checks '>=1 successful run' — historically true; the report's close-listing covers only security/gate:confirmed-high closes since baseline (design point 4), so a non-floored P0 laundered close appears NOWHERE; the report's audit section is the stale last-good summary, which the design never requires to be fresh. (5) The one human signs an honest-looking report; the gate greens over a laundered close with zero of the three claimed defenses (nightly repair, report visibility, human witness) ever engaging. This is the load-bearing architectural gap, not an edge case: the proposal's whole bet is 'detection-and-reopen dominates prevention-by-predicate', yet the detector's liveness is the one thing the predicate layer never checks. Aggravator from the same text: the migration mass-closes hundreds of design-superseded findings without merged closing PRs, which the auditor's own heuristics (a)/(b) are written to REOPEN on first contact — so the bootstrap run either triggers a reopen storm back into criteria 1–5 or the heuristics get quietly weakened, which is how the liveness gap becomes permanent.

best_spine: dx-first's thin current-state gate with one verified human signature is the only skeleton this loop can actually build and run this sprint — but the synthesis must promote auditor liveness (green run within N hours of gate time, over the full window since baseline) into a blocking gate criterion, adopt contract-first's pure decide(evidence)->verdict core plus fixture suite for exactly the predicates that remain (with fixtures generated FROM real collector output, never hand-transcribed prose), and replace security-first's unsatisfiable roster-history walk with the roster hash pinned in the synthesis ADR.
